description: We are a multidisciplinary technical team from Comodoro Rivadavia, specializing in electromechanics, electronics, and software development. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we developed "explore, understand and reclaim", a web platform that transforms abandoned space hardware on the Moon and Mars into a strategic resource for a circular economy (ISRU)—by combining NASA orbital data, 3D modeling, and intelligent assistance for recovery engineering.
summary: South Cosmos is an interactive web-based planetary environmental analogy and simulation tool designed to evaluate and compare terrain, atmospheric, and compositional variables across celestial bodies (Earth, Mars, and the Moon). Developed using React, TypeScript, Three.js, and Python backend algorithms, the tool processes continuous environmental data (temperature, pressure, wind, light, gravity, radiation) to compute percentage-based similarity scores. By functioning as an analytical toolkit that bridges terrestrial analogs (such as Atacama) with extraterrestrial sites, South Cosmos helps researchers and engineers model and validate robotic systems under extreme conditions. This instrument is crucial for advancing mission planning, optimizing rover hardware testing, and democratizing access to planetary science data.
details:
• What it does & How it works: South Cosmos functions as an exploratory computational simulation tool rather than a closed-loop simulator. Its core engine (analogo.py) ingests and processes environmental and compositional metrics across planetary bodies to calculate percentage-based similarities using continuous variables, daily cycles, and safety penalty algorithms. The interactive frontend provides real-time satellite maps (GoogleSatelliteMap, PlanetarySatelliteMap), 3D viewport rendering (Wear3DViewport, WearTestStudio), time-series graphs (TimeSeriesPanel), and machine learning integrations (MlPanel) to help users analyze environmental dynamics and analog fidelity.
    • Languages & Frameworks: Python, TypeScript, React, HTML5, CSS3, SQL.
    • Libraries & Engines: NumPy, Three.js, Express, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Firebase.
    • Software & Development Environments: Node.js, Git, Arduino IDE.
    • Hardware: Standard workstation architecture utilized for numerical modeling, testing, and web application deployment.
  • Creativity & Innovation: South Cosmos innovates as a modular tool by combining real-time multi-variable weighting with critical hazard penalization formulas. Rather than acting as a static simulator, it features automated data ingestion cycles (ciclo.py), relational database tracking (db.py), and immersive 3D/geographic visualizations that serve as a practical toolkit for scientific exploration.
  • Team Considerations: The development prioritized modularity, open-source repairability, computational efficiency (relying on NumPy for core vector calculations), and clean, uncluttered human-designed interfaces tailored for scientific clarity.
